text: Version 4 is issued in Draft: no approval is recorded for this version.
why: The WP gives no approver and no approval record for the next version; the run proceeds without a human approval stop (D-RCV-60 overlay; Template and Rules §R1 U8).
read: The source version 3 metadata table, the WP and the run rules
impact: The document is usable for build and review; a formal approval remains open.

text: The transactional outbox and the inbox apply to all 19 services in the target, and the Epic 1 and Epic 2 wording of version 3 is kept as the as-built position.
why: Arch v5 and DP-09 give every service an outbox and an inbox; version 3 limits the outbox to Epics 1 and 2. R-PREC puts Arch v5 first.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 22; DP-09; ADR-015
applied_in: Section 1 Rules, last bullet; section 6, outbox bullet
impact: Every service's DB and event story includes the outbox and inbox library objects.

text: The retry ladder is 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and then the .dlt topic of the owner's topic, and each of the 19 services owns the retry and dead-letter topics of its own topic until the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog names them.
why: Arch v5 gives the ladder and the .dlt rule but no topic names; Template and Rules §R4 requires retry and .dlt topics for every service topic.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 22; Template and Rules v1 §R4; Microservice Ownership Map v1 Services and Events sheets
impact: The names are placeholders until the naming library and the topic catalog are issued; no code depends on a name yet.

text: A REST hop timeout shows an RFC 9457 problem detail on the panel that needed it and changes no case state, and no message ID is added for it in this standard.
why: Arch v5 gives RFC 9457 problem details for REST errors and the standard adds no message code; the user-facing wording for this new failure category is not in version 3.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 11; version 3 A43
impact: Screens show the problem detail; a message code can be added later without a design change.

text: The platform administrator receives the .dlt alert and runs the replay tool; the owning service fixes the cause.
why: Arch v5 gives an alert and a replay tool but no role; version 3 already gives the platform administrator the outbound queue and the workflow failures.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 22; version 3 A24
impact: The alert routing and the replay rights are set in the observability design and the access model.

text: The 2 s is the ceiling of one REST call and 1.2 s is the planning figure for the composed screen against the 2 s p95 target.
why: Arch v5 gives 2 s to each hop and 2 s to the screen, planned at about 1.2 s, and does not say which figure is the ceiling.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (budget 0.15 s + 0.6 s + 0.3 s)
impact: The performance test asserts a 2 s per-call ceiling and a 2 s p95 screen target with a 1.2 s plan.
